transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling really unsettled. When I’m walking across campus, it’s like I’m seeing everything through glass. I don’t feel fully in my own body, and the buildings and students around me seem a little unreal. That’s been scaring me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About six days. It started after the lighting rig collapsed during the showcase, and it’s been going on since then.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that aren't there since the incident?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen anything that wasn’t actually there. It’s more that things feel unreal, not that I’m seeing things.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the incident?
Yes. I feel really on edge. If a door bangs or a cart rattles in the hallway, I jump so hard my chest hurts, and then it takes me a few minutes to stop shaking and get back to what I was doing.
Have you been avoiding any places, activities, or situations since the lighting rig collapsed?

Yes. I’ve been going the long way around campus so I don’t have to walk past the atrium. And if someone brings up the showcase, I usually change the subject or just leave before I have to talk about it.
Do you feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or as if you're in a dream when these unsettling feelings happen?

Yes. That’s actually one of the scariest parts. When I’m walking across campus, it feels like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not fully in my own body. The buildings and students around me seem slightly unreal, almost dreamlike.
Have you had any memory problems or gaps in your memory since the incident with the lighting rig?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been distracted, but I haven’t noticed any actual gaps in my memory or parts of the incident that I can’t remember.
Has your feeling unsettled and the things seeming unreal been affecting your ability to do your daily activities or interact with friends and family?

Yes, it has. I haven’t been able to do my job normally. I walked out of a planning meeting because I just couldn’t stay in the room, and I’ve missed two mentoring sessions with students. I’m also avoiding parts of campus I’m supposed to use, so it’s definitely getting in the way.
Do you feel like you're reliving the moment when the lighting rig collapsed when you experience these unsettling feelings?

Yes. It’s like the moment comes back suddenly. I’ll be grading or just making coffee, and the sound of the rig coming down barges into my head. Then I can see the volunteer on the floor and the students pushing forward, like it’s happening right in front of me again.
Are there any specific people you've been avoiding since the lighting rig collapsed?

Not really specific people, I guess. It’s more the place and the topic. I’ve been taking the long way around campus so I don’t have to pass the atrium, and if anyone brings up the showcase, I change the subject or leave before I have to talk about it.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family since the incident?

Yes. My husband has been trying to help, and I can tell he’s being kind, but I’m not really responding like I normally would. He cut flowers from the garden and made me tea, and I knew it was sweet, but I just felt… blank. Heavy. I couldn’t feel the warmth or comfort I usually would.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to the lighting rig collapsing during the showcase?
I’m not sure I’d call it guilt. I keep wondering if there was something I should have noticed or done faster, but I don’t really know. Mostly I just feel shaken when I think about it.
Do you find yourself trying to push away or avoid thoughts, memories, or feelings related to the lighting rig collapsing?

Yes. I try not to think about it if I can. I’ll take the long way around campus so I don’t have to go near the atrium, and if someone starts talking about the showcase, I usually change the subject or just leave.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy since the incident with the lighting rig?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way. I haven’t been doing much, but I don’t know if that’s because I’ve lost interest or because I just don’t feel up to it right now.
Have you been having any negative thoughts about yourself or others since the incident?

I don’t think so, not in a strong way. I’ve been upset and kind of hard on myself at times, but I haven’t noticed myself thinking badly about other people or feeling like everyone’s unsafe or anything like that.
Have you noticed any significant difficulties in your relationships with friends, family, or at work since the incident?

Yes, mostly with work. I haven’t been able to do my job normally. I walked out of a planning meeting because I just couldn’t stay in the room, and I missed two mentoring sessions with students. I’m also avoiding parts of campus that I’m supposed to use, so it’s starting to get in the way.
Have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy doing since the incident with the lighting rig?

I’m not really sure. I’ve been doing less of the things I normally do, but I can’t tell if I’ve lost interest or if I’m just distracted and worn out. I haven’t noticed a clear change like “I don’t enjoy this anymore.”
